@graph.name: Dataset Catalog Registry — Operations
@graph.description: The operations record for the dataset catalog registry of The Flat Rate Movers: what the registry is, the seats it joins, and the gates that verify it. The registry is the dataset-catalog element (Element 4) of the Retrieval Machine, built from Dossier 04 §5: one joined, computed view of every dataset file the company publishes and every catalog that carries it — the company website, the estate API, the GitHub AI repository, two Hugging Face dataset repositories, the Zenodo DOI deposit, and Google Dataset Search — plus the channels deliberately not used, recorded with their reasons. Presence and version-sync states are computed from primary reads at every generation and sealed in the signed master index; nothing in the file is asserted without a dated observation behind it.

@graph.name: Dataset Catalog Registry — Scope Rules
@graph.description: The scope rules of the catalog registry: the join is datasets x seats with exactly one row per dataset per applicable seat; the presence vocabulary (present-verified, absent-observed, present-stale, not-submitted, not-applicable, and unverified-on-read-failure); the sync-computation rule (digests compared, never asserted; an unreadable seat computes stale-unknown); the evidence rule (every present-verified row carries a dated observation with a method); the metadata-completeness encoding in the verify.js DC vocabulary; the DOI discipline (DOIs as data fields only, never as node identifiers); and self-inclusion (the registry joins its own seats with computed states).

scopeRules.text: The join is datasets x seats: every dataset file that is a distribution of the signed master index (plus this registry file itself) carries exactly one row for each of the seven seats: website, api, github-ai, huggingface-estate, huggingface-intent, zenodo, dataset-search. The two non-channel catalogs (kaggle, data-gov) carry catalog rows only and never join rows. Gate CR-1 verifies completeness in both directions at every seal.

presence_state is one of: present-verified (a dated observation with a method stands behind the row), absent-observed (a dated read found the file missing), present-stale (present and read, but not the current generation — used where a seat reports presence without per-file digests), not-submitted (a channel with a submission step that has not been taken), not-applicable (the seat does not carry this file by design), or unverified (read failed) — a read failure is recorded as an observation and the row’s sync state computes to stale-unknown; presence is never upgraded on a failed read.

version_sync_state is computed, never asserted: file seats compare SHA-256 digests (mirror copy vs the signed master index digest); repository seats compare git blob SHA-1 (mirror blob vs local file); the API seat reads the refresh-bundle manifest’s digest-match record. A seat whose digest cannot be read computes to stale-unknown, never to current.

Every present-verified row carries presenceEvidence {method, observedAt, source}. A claim without a dated observation behind it does not ship: it degrades to the honest state (absent-observed, present-stale, or stale-unknown) instead.

Website and dataset-search rows carry metadata_completeness in the verify.js DC vocabulary: DC-1 (every Dataset node description within 50–5,000 characters), DC-3 (dateModified not before datePublished), DC-4 (creator/publisher the canonical Organization) computed per file at generation; DC-2 and DC-5 recorded as suite-gate verdicts with the per-file DOI content scans computed. datasets-videos.json is not-applicable for DC-1/DC-4 (its graph is VideoObject-typed) and the row says why.

DOIs appear in this file as data fields and prose facts only. No Dataset or DataCatalog node in this file carries a DOI in its identifier (gate CR-4): the software concept DOI stays on exactly its lawful holder nodes estate-wide, and the dataset concept DOI stays on the collection node at /datasets/#collection.

This registry file is a row subject like every other dataset file: it joins all seven seats with its own computed states, including the honest ones (absent from snapshot seats until their next refresh, and trailing itself by one generation on mirror seats by construction).

@graph.name: Dataset Catalog Registry — The Catalogs
@graph.description: The nine catalog rows: seven channels that carry or can carry the estate’s datasets (the company website, the estate API, the GitHub AI repository, the Hugging Face estate repository, the Hugging Face intent repository, the Zenodo DOI deposit, and Google Dataset Search) and two channels recorded as not pursued by design with their re-entry conditions (Kaggle, data.gov). Each row states the channel kind, its URL, exactly what it distributes, its status and the date it was last observed — including the honest states: the Zenodo deposit is a stale snapshot by design, and the Hugging Face seats’ current read state is recorded as it stands.

catalogs.name: The Flat Rate Movers website (canonical)
catalogs.distributionScope: Every dataset file is published at the site root and sealed in the signed master index; dataset landings under /datasets/<name>/ are generated per file. At this generation the live bundle lists 45 of 47 files; a file published after the last refresh joins at the next batch close.

catalogs.distributionScope: The dataset deposit is a versioned snapshot zip (the-flat-rate-movers-datasets-2026-11-02.zip), not a live mirror: at this generation’s read it holds 38 of 47 dataset files, 0 digest-current. A new-version deposit at the next release is the recorded remedy (gap C2). The record’s concept DOI is the citable dataset DOI; it is carried here as data fields only and never as an identifier of any node in this file (gate CR-4).

catalogs.name: Google Dataset Search
catalogs.distributionScope: Dataset Search has no submission or API: presence is earned by crawl of the landings’ Dataset markup and read back only by querying the surface. The estate-level recorded state is absent (full audits 2026-10-30 and 2026-10-31, sampled re-checks since); per-dataset presence is not observable on this surface (gap CR-G2), so join rows carry the estate-level state with the audit dates as evidence.

catalogs.name: Kaggle Datasets
catalogs.distributionScope: No Kaggle dataset exists and none is claimed. The channel is mapped here so the catalog map is complete: every channel considered carries a row, including the ones deliberately not used.
catalogs.reEntryConditions: Re-enters only if the owner personally creates and signs in to a Kaggle account and asks for the mirror (account creation is an owner step under the registry login-route rule); the mirror then publishes under the same CC BY 4.0 license with the signed index as its provenance.

catalogs.name: data.gov
catalogs.distributionScope: No data.gov listing exists and none is claimed. data.gov catalogs United States government datasets; a private company’s commercial dataset estate is outside its collection scope, so the channel is recorded as mapped-and-declined rather than left as an unexamined blank.
catalogs.reEntryConditions: Re-enters only if a government partner program or an agency data call makes a private-sector listing in scope; no action is pending and none is scheduled.

@graph.name: Dataset Catalog Registry — Method
@graph.description: How this registry is generated and how to read it: the generator (scripts/build-catalog-registry.js, a Flat Rate Machine tool) derives the dataset set from the signed master index, reads every seat from its primary source, computes presence and sync, merges the append-only observation store, and writes this file; verify.js gates CR-1..CR-5 check the join’s completeness, its evidence, its digest backing, its DOI discipline and its diagnostic order at every seal.
@graph.articleBody: Generation. The generator reads the signed master index (ai-master-index.json) for the authoritative dataset-file set (adding this registry file itself), reads each file’s bytes from the Pages tree, and computes metadata completeness per file in the DC vocabulary (descriptions measured, date order compared, creator/publisher matched against the canonical Organization; DOI content scans for the DC-5 record). Seat reads: website = local SHA-256 vs the signed index digest; api = live GET /v1/datasets for presence plus the refresh-bundle manifest’s per-file digest record for sync; github-ai = the local mirror clone’s origin/main tree after fetch, git blob SHA-1 vs the local file; huggingface = Hub API recursive tree reads through the estate’s connector, blob SHA-1 vs the local file — on 2026-11-04 every Hub read failed with HTTP 401, so both seats compute stale-unknown with the failure recorded as an observation (the seats’ last verified state, 2026-11-02, stands in the catalogs node); zenodo = the dataset-line deposit zip downloaded and hashed per file; dataset-search = the recorded estate-level audits (the surface exposes no per-dataset signal). Observations merge from the append-only store data/catalog-observations.json plus this run’s seat summaries, deduped; the store is appended in the same motion. Reading the join. presence_state answers "is it there" with its evidence attached; version_sync_state answers "is the copy current" and is only ever a digest comparison result — current, stale, stale-unknown (digest unreadable), or null where the seat carries no per-file digest. Self-inclusion honesty: this file’s own mirror-seat rows describe the previous sealed generation, because a registry cannot contain its own final digest; the post-close comparisons land in the batch record and in the next generation. Cadence: regenerated at every estate release and at each monthly observation append; the E6-B3 batch wires the runner with the observation store as its home (gap C5).

boundaryRules.text: Presence is observed or it is not claimed. Snapshot seats (Zenodo) and crawl-earned surfaces (Dataset Search) show their true states — absent and stale rows are published, not rounded up.

This registry creates no account and submits nothing anywhere. Channels that need an owner sign-in (Kaggle) are recorded not-pursued-by-design with their re-entry conditions; account steps are owner steps.

No listing, indexing, ranking or citation by any third-party catalog is claimed beyond what a dated observation in this file records. Dataset Search presence in particular is reported as the recorded estate-level observation, never as per-dataset fact (gap CR-G2).

Mirror seats are copies of the canonical website files; the canonical provenance is the signed master index on theflatratemovers.com. A stale mirror is a distribution lag with a recorded remedy (the next refresh), never a second source of truth.

This registry describes published dataset files and public catalogs only. Internal research stores (buyer intelligence, quote records, client material) are not dataset files, appear in no catalog, and are never described here.
